NIT Rourkela Scientist Honoured with INSA Associate Fellowship!

Prof. Bhaskar Kundu, Associate Professor in the Department of Earth and Atmospheric Sciences at the National Institute of Technology Rourkela, has been selected as an 'INSA Associate Fellow (IAF) for the year 2026' by the Indian National Science Academy (INSA).

Notably, Prof. Kundu is the only scientist selected in the field of Earth & Environmental Sciences by the INSA Sectional Committee for the prestigious recognition this year, highlighting the significance of his research contributions at the national level.

Prof. Kundu has been recognized for his outstanding contributions in solid earth geophysics, particularly in the areas of kinematic and dynamic modelling. His research has significantly advanced the understanding of various geodynamic and geological processes in Central India. Prof. Kundu, who is also a Humboldt Research Fellow, has established himself as a leading researcher through academic excellence, impactful publications, and significant contributions to teaching and scientific advancement.

INSA established in 1935 under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, is the country’s apex scientific body representing all branches of science and technology. Initiated in 2024, the 'INSA Associate Fellows (IAF)' programme recognizes outstanding mid-career scientists for their notable contributions to science, engineering, medicine, and technology. Each year, a maximum of 20 scientists are selected through a rigorous evaluation process conducted by specialized INSA Sectional Committees.
